newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese banks' capital to reach $1 bln in Dec.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese banks' capital to reach $1 bln in Dec.

text.p: The total capital of Lebanon's commercial banks will reach $1 billion by the end of 1996, Bank of Lebanon Governor Riad Salameh said on Tuesday.
Salameh said the banks' capital was $260 million at the end of 1993.

He told bankers at an "Arab Banks and Economic Reform Conference" in Beirut that the total capital of Lebanese banks "rose to $910 million by October 1996 and this capital is expected to reach $1 billion by year end".
He said an essential goal of the central bank over the past few years was to encourage banks to increase their capital. There are 82 commercial banks in Lebanon.

"The Bank of Lebanon worked to make this increase cover all banks, so it issued circulars setting the minimum capital for the main headquarters of any bank working in Lebanon at 10 billion Lebanese pounds and 250 million pounds for a branch," he added.
Salameh said the rule would take effect at the end of 1997 and would affect both Lebanese banks and the Lebanon branches of foreign banks.
